requirements.text: The system shall allow users to spatially and temporally track and analyze Regulatory and Resource Management data.
The system shall integrate data from the Regulatory Database (RDB), Water Management Database (WMDB), and GIS.
The system shall support the tracking of lapsed quantities, including identification of the permit, well, location, reason for lapse, and MFL zone.
The system shall provide tools to track and report on net benefit changes, including relocated permits, land use changes, and water withdrawal credits.
The system shall allow users to generate reports on permit history, including use type, irrigated acres, and pumpage.
The system shall provide a map interface to visualize permit locations, heat maps of over-pumping, and MFL cones of depression.
The system shall allow users to search for and view water use permits by various criteria such as issue date, expiration date, use type, and permit status.
The system shall support the generation of well packages for use in groundwater modeling.
The system shall allow authorized users to maintain business rule parameters, water use estimates, and system news.
The system shall implement role-based security to control access to features and data.
The system shall provide reasonable response times for queries and map rendering to support statutory permitting time frames.
The system shall perform nightly database replication from the IBM DB2 mainframe to the read-only Oracle database.
The system shall provide an intuitive web-based interface with online help and documentation.
The system shall be developed using the District's existing hardware and software architecture, including ArcGIS, ArcIMS, and .NET technologies.
